newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagreb bourse hopes for new listings to prop trade.
newsitem.headline: Zagreb bourse hopes for new listings to prop trade.

text.p: Croatia's central bourse hopes for new listings soon to attract investors and bolster trickling trade, its director Marinko Papuga said on Thursday.
"We are pleased to have our three bravest (companies) in top listing now and hope others will also take this step to promote our market," Papuga told a news conference.
The Zagreb Stock Exchange has just signed an agreement moving one of the leading commercial banks, Varazdinska Banka, to the top stock bracket alongside drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka.
Another strong regional bank and some of the most attractive companies from other sectors are now also readying business results and other documents required for full listing.
Such moves were described by officials and analysts as "highly commendable" and likely to reawaken interest in the almost dormant share market.
Turnover has dropped to meagre levels of a few million kuna a day after two bull runs last October and January this year saw business booming.
It had spurred the bourse to work on upgrading its trading system to cope with an increasing number of transactions.
A lack of reliable information is thought to be the main stumbling block for foreign buyers and fund managers, cautiously testing the Croatian investment climate.

Papuga also blamed it for causing a drastic reduction in deals recently as investors withheld their orders for most firms trading in the bourse's semi-regulated segment, but also for two market heavyweights.
But the bourse now mulls tightening disclosure rules for all firms in a bid to improve transparency. It is also pushing for speedier clearing and settlement to spur trading.
"There will also be some other rules and changes to minimum capital requirement for brokerages -- it is something that potential foreign clients are asking for," Papuga told Reuters.
